blocks.text: This page tracks the Coquitlam MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $957,500 for a typical home, down 7.1% over twelve months.
Coquitlam benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Coquitlam home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $957,500 in October 2026. That is down 1.5% on the month, down 3.0% over three months, down 4.1% over six months and down 7.1% over the year. Over three years it is down 13.5%, and over five years down 7.5%.
The weakest one-year move in Coquitlam was for an apartment homes at −9.1%; the strongest was a townhouse at −6.6%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,571,400) and an apartment ($624,200) is $947,200, and a townhouse ($962,600) sits $338,400 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Coquitlam is 10.4% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 7.1% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Coquitlam ranks 14 by all-home benchmark, with Burnaby East above it at $972,500 and Burnaby North below it at $875,000.

Detached homes in Coquitlam: benchmark $1,571,400, little changed at −0.8% in a month, down 3.5% in three months, down 3.9% in six months, down 7.0% in a year, down 12.1% in three years and down 3.3% in five. That is 11.5% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Coquitlam: benchmark $962,600, little changed at −1.4% in a month, down 2.8% in three months, down 4.5% in six months, down 6.6% in a year, down 9.2% in three years and up 3.3% in five. That is 4.4% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Coquitlam: benchmark $624,200, down 2.5% in a month, down 4.2% in three months, down 6.0% in six months, down 9.1% in a year, down 13.8% in three years and down 2.4% in five. That is 7.3% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Coquitlam home is worth about $73,200 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,030,700. By type, detached homes lost about $118,300, from $1,689,700 to $1,571,400, townhouses lost about $68,000, from $1,030,600 to $962,600, and apartments lost about $62,500, from $686,700 to $624,200 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $998,400 six months ago and near $1,106,900 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $40,900 below the six-month mark and about $149,400 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Coquitlam benchmark is about $111,100 below the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $96,500 below.
The $957,500 Coquitlam figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Coquitlam home was $957,500, with detached at $1,571,400.
